title: How AI Learns to Answer with Help

sections.heading: Everyday Analogy
sections.body:
Think of AI like a new helper in a library.

Generative AI (an AI that creates text, images, or video from what it learned) is like a helper who read many books and can write new answers.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is when that helper is allowed to look up fresh books before answering, so answers are more current and true.

A RAG Agent is a helper that can do steps on its own: search, check, then answer.

CUDA programming means teaching the helper to use many small calculators at once (a GPU) to work faster.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body:
We want AI that is useful in the real world.

- Video AI applications let AI watch and understand video, like finding objects in security footage.
- Edge AI on Jetson Nano means running AI on a tiny device itself, not in the cloud, so it works fast even without internet.
- Digital fingerprinting adds a hidden mark to AI-made content so we can tell what is real and protect it.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body:
Even good helpers break.

If the lookup books are wrong, RAG will give wrong answers with confidence.

If video AI gets too much video, it slows down and needs more GPU power.

If digital fingerprints are removed or faked, we lose trust in what AI made.

Small devices like Jetson Nano can overheat or run out of memory if asked to do too much.

steps.narration: You ask a question that needs current facts.
RAG searches documents to find true info before answering.
CUDA on the GPU processes lots of data quickly.
The RAG Agent combines search and generation to answer.
The answer can run as a Video AI app or on a Jetson Nano device.

quiz.q: What does RAG do for an AI helper?
options: Lets it look up fresh documents before answering
Removes the need for any training data
quiz.why: RAG means Retrieval-Augmented Generation - the AI retrieves real documents to make answers more current and true.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x on a Video AI app?
options: GPU runs out of power and slows down
quiz.why: Video AI needs heavy processing. With 100x more video, the GPU/CUDA system hits limits, causing slowdowns, delays, and dropped frames.

quiz.q: Why use Edge AI on Jetson Nano?
options: To run AI directly on a small device without always needing the cloud
To make AI unable to process video
quiz.why: Edge AI lets the device itself run AI quickly, even offline, which is good for real devices like cameras or robots.

extra: GPU stands for Graphics Processing Unit, originally for graphics but now widely used for AI.
